thing.text:
RESORT INFINITY

Everything is out the back
door: the cottages, the front
desk, the guests.

Go outside.

thing.note: The resort’s own machinery, which you never need to touch: six behaviours, one per guest, three robots each. SPACE here is the six guests arriving at once — they write to the post and walk to their cottages as soon as a clerk answers. Nothing in them knows how many guests there are.
Guest 1’s own three robots: ask the desk where to live, walk to the cottage it is given, and ask again when the bell rings. They work on guest 1, and on nothing else.

active.name: Ask for a place

team.name: Move on the bell I kept
team.note: The bell rang before I had a place, and the pad was kept in hole 7. Now that I have one: the same as Move when told to, on the kept pad.

team.name: Move when told to
team.note: A pad has landed on my nest: the bell, rung for every guest. Sends [where I live, my own bird] to the moving office and takes my place out of the box, so that the answer puts a new one in.

team.name: Keep the bell for later
team.note: The bell rang before I had a place (Move when told to did not fit): takes the pad off my nest into hole 7, which uncovers the address under it.

team.name: Stand at my address
team.note: A number has landed on my nest: that is my address. Works out where that cottage stands along the row, remembers it as my place, and walks there.

active.note: Leads. My number is still in the box, so I have nowhere to live: sends [my number, my own bird] to the desk and takes my number out as it goes, so I never ask twice.

holes.name: Tidy
holes.note: Rides in the little house behind your robot: once your robot has answered the letter, sweeps the empty letter away, and the house folds itself up.

active.name: Run your robot on the letter

team.name: Take the robot in
team.note: A robot has landed on its nest: yours. Takes it into hole 2.

active.note: A letter lies on the post and your robot is in hole 2: takes a fresh little house, puts the letter in it, then a copy of your robot with a copy of Tidy behind it, and sets the house down on the grass to work.

thing.text:
RESORT INFINITY

You are the clerk. Eleven
cottages stand in a row,
numbered from the left. Guests
arrive at the gate; every
guest needs a cottage, and no
two may share one.

The guests write to the FRONT
DESK, the house by the gate.
The desk answers with a robot
of yours: a robot given a
letter, [number | bird], that
gives the bird the cottage
number. Train it, and give it
to the bird "to the front
desk". The desk does the rest.

Set the Speed to 4x or 8x: a
resort takes a while at
walking pace.

PROBLEM 1
The first infinite group

Six guests wait at the gate,
numbered 1 to 6, and more are
behind them for ever.

Point at the pad "the guests",
hand empty, and press SPACE:
every guest writes to the
front desk, [my number |
bird], and waits.

Train a robot that answers
with a cottage number (see
HOW TO TRAIN ONE), pick it up
and give it to the bird "to
the front desk". Or give her
"Next address", by the fence.
Each guest walks to its
cottage.

Which cottage should guest 1
have?

HOW TO TRAIN ONE

Take a little robot from its
stack and set it on the grass.
Drop a practice letter ON it:
its thought bubble opens and
you are teaching it.

Problem 1: click the number,
then click the bird: it flies
to the practice nest.
Problem 2: take a number from
the stack, type 5, drop it on
the letter’s number; then the
number to the bird.

Ruby erases the number in its
thought: any number will do.
Leave the bubble, click the
robot to pick it up, and give
it to the bird.

PROBLEM 2
Five more, and no room

Five more guests arrive and
every cottage is taken. Nobody
is turned away: everybody
housed moves along, and the
newcomers take 1 to 5.

Train a robot that, given
[where a guest lives | bird],
gives the bird where to move
to. Give it to the bird "to
the moving office": the
office rings the bell, every
housed guest writes where it
lives, and your robot answers
each. Then SPACE on "five
more guests".

Why does this work here, and
not in a hundred-room hotel?

THE ROW GOES ON

Eleven cottages stand in a
row, counted from the left,
and a guest given a number
walks to that cottage.

The row does not stop at the
fence: guest 12 would walk
past it, and guest a thousand
a long way past.

Nothing in these robots knows
how many guests there are.
That is the whole of it.

thing.name: Next address
thing.note: Problem 1, answered: guest i lives at cottage i. Given a [number | bird] letter, takes the number and gives it to the bird.

thing.name: Move up five
thing.note: Problem 2, answered: everybody moves up five, which empties cottages 1 to 5 for the newcomers. Given a [where I live | bird] letter, drops a +5 on the number, takes it and gives it to the bird.
